messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired: capacity_exhaustion.alert for service=renderer-queue in prod-us-west. queue_depth=124k, processing_rate=180r/s, target_rate=1000r/s, autoscaler_status=stalled :rotating_light:
pagerduty: INCIDENT: P123456 - prod-us-west renderer queue backlog — triggered 08:03 UTC
Alex M: acked. I’m on it. grabbing logs now.
Priya R: I’m waking up, ETA ~2m. any customer impact reported?
Alex M: internal metrics: tail latency spiked to 12s for generation calls. error rate from gateway ~0.8% 5m window. most requests queuing.
SRE Oncall: autoscaler controller shows repeated scale_crash errors, pod create failing with ImagePullBackOff? but cluster nodes have free GPU allocatable.
James K: I see k8s events: failed scheduling due to taint:gpu-preemptible not tolerated on new nodes. recently applied nodepool change last night.
Priya R: can we flip to burst pool? there’s an emergency surge pool we can enable manually.
Alex M: trying a manual scale: `kubectl scale deployment/renderer-workers --replicas=40 -n prod`
Alex M: scaling command returned success but new pods stuck in pending with message: "0/12 nodes are available: 12 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector."
Priya R: that confirms nodeSelector mismatch. we rolled a nodepool label change during maintenance. rolling back nodeSelector is risky mid-prod.
SRE Oncall: mitigation plan: 1) enable fallback model variant (qqm-7b) for low-priority routes to reduce GPU memory and increase throughput, 2) enable emergency-burst nodepool (manual), 3) temporarily shed non-critical background jobs.
James K: I can toggle the emergency-burst pool. making the change now: `gcloud container node-pools create burst-pool --machine-type n1-standard-16 --num-nodes 6 --labels ginger=burst`
Alex M: also flipping routing rule to send 20% traffic to hosted-fallback to reduce load: updating envoy route config.
Priya R: implementing fallback model switch for routes /generate-bulk and /embeddings-batch. patching infra config: `set-model-variant --service renderer --variant qqm-7b --routes /generate-bulk,/embeddings-batch`
incident-bot: PagerDuty update: P123456 acknowledged by Alex M (08:05 UTC). escalation to senior oncall in 5m if not resolved.
James K: burst-pool creation completed. nodes are Ready. scheduling should work now.
Alex M: new pods coming up, some still failing init due to missing configMap key `GPU_ACCEL`. applying quick patch.
Priya R: configMap patched. pods are Ready. processing rate recovered to ~720r/s and queue depth dropping (now 32k).
SRE Oncall: Latency back to ~250ms p50 for small prompts, p95 ~1.8s. we still have backlog but draining.
Alex M: routing drop applied, fallback variant handling ~18% of traffic. overall throughput ~820r/s.
Priya R: customer-visible errors dropped to 0.1%. no direct customer pages yet but some retries observed from high-volume customers.
James K: created an emergency rollback to previous nodepool labels and opened a ticket with infra to audit the nodeSelector change.
Alex M: marking this as mitigated for paging. will keep thread open for handoff and postmortem items.
SRE Oncall: escalation canceled (pagerduty). I'll run a quick post-incident checklist: collect events, pod logs, autoscaler controller logs, cluster change from last 24h. Assigning postmortem leads: Alex M, Priya R.
Priya R: noted. adding action items: 1) add guardrail to prevent nodepool label removal from prod node selector, 2) make emergency-burst toggle a runbook step with one-click button in console, 3) make autoscaler more resilient to missing labels.
Alex M: saving logs: `/var/log/renderer/autoscaler-2026-02-14.log` and k8s events to S3 bucket s3://redwood-incident-logs/P123456/
incident-bot: Incident P123456 status changed to acknowledged -> resolved at 08:18 UTC (automated).
James K: creating follow-up RFC for nodepool-label safety and a playbook for manual burst creation.
Priya R: great work team. will draft postmortem and circulate for 48h review. :thumbsup:
Alex M: thanks. handing off to Priya for postmortem writeup. I’ll update the runbook with the commands we used.
SRE Oncall: thread closed for active mitigation. keeping watchers until queue depth <1k.
Alex M: queue depth now 980. leaving final note: root cause = nodepool label change + missing guardrail in autoscaler logic, contributed to delayed scaling and queue pileup.
Priya R: final: incident severity set to Sev2. tagging impacted customers and notifying support to prepare comms.
